text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Swedish newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Large doses of vitamin E may slow the deterioration caused by Alzheimer's disease, U.S. research shows.
- Shares in Pharmacia & Upjohn dived 39 crowns to 230 crowns on the Stockholm stock exchange on Wednesday after the company once again lowered its profit forecast.

- Scandinavian Airlines SAS risks having to pay 150 million crowns if former unit Premiair loses a court case. Former Scanair employees not hired when Scanair became Premiair are claiming damages, saying Premiair did not follow labour market regulations when choosing which employees could stay on. SAS has made provisions of less than 100 million crowns for the court case.
- An upturn on the stock exchange and an increased rateable value on houses mean more people have to pay wealth taxes, which in turn means some shareholders have to pay for holding shares.
- Shares in drugs company Pharmacia & Upjohn dropped 15 percent after the group issued a profit warning.
- Swedish companies turned less optimistic in April after having indicated growing optimism for a year, according to a survey by pollster Skop.

- Pharmacia & Upjohn shares plunge after another profits warning. It said that first quarter sales would be down 16 percent. The profits warning is the latest in a string of setbacks, including complaints about the disclosure of information to the markets, the sudden resignation of its former CEO and the rising costs of the merger that formed the group.

- Broker Hagstromer and Qviberg says the Swedish IT sector is expanding at a rate of 40 percent a year although its shares have also gained rapidly. Only two of the nine quoted firms, Intentia and Resco, are rated as buys by the broker.

- Defence contractor Kockums may get a new partner in the Australian Submarine Corporation (ASC), in which it holds a 49 percent stake. The newspaper cites reports as saying that Australian industrialist Richard Pratt wants to buy into ASC.

- A medical analyst says that calcium antagonist blood pressure medicine, which is among the drugs made by Pharmacia and Astra, make people more suicidal. Astra says its data shows no such side-effects.
- The newspaper says that Danish conglomerate A.P. Moeller wants to keep a low profile as it does not give details about a whole range of minor subsidiaries in its annual report.
